name: Woodsee safety policy
description: Machine-enforced protective defaults. Applied by the installer, git hooks and the safety CLI.

rules.action: Run lib/scanner.py quick then deep on all downloaded source before any setup/build command. The deep stage runs ClamAV automatically when clamscan is installed, and --clamav makes it mandatory.
Refuse to copy vendored source containing home paths, machine names, key-shaped strings, private IPs or emails.
Create a timestamped .bak copy before modifying any user config or preference file.
Merge managed entries into existing configs; never replace the whole file or drop entries you did not add.
No API keys, tokens, passwords or private IPs in source, configs, logs or memory. Use Keychain or environment variables.
Full secret + PII scan of all staged files before any public push. The name 'woodsee' is explicitly allowed.
Scrubbing must provide a real redaction mode (safety.py scrub --fix) with a verified backup per file, not only a report telling the user to fix it manually.

Deny rm -rf /, mkfs, newfs, dd, shred, srm, diskutil erase/partition, chmod -R 000, chown -R, kill -9, killall, pkill -9, shutdown, reboot, halt. Require explicit confirmation for other rm/mv/kill/rmdir operations.
Verification stops at build success. Do not open, launch, kill or UI-drive the app - the user tests it themselves.
Make a recoverable backup and confirm it succeeded before touching preferences, keychain items, model files or project config.
New original repos use PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; forks keep their upstream licence.
Prefer local/offline tools and local models. Avoid telemetry, analytics and unnecessary cloud calls.
Do not initialise git inside iCloud-synced folders. Prefer offline local repos with no remote until explicitly requested.
